title: CXL-ECC: an Efficient LRC-based on-CXL-Memory-eXpander-Controller ECC to Enhance Reliability and Performance of DRAM Error Correction
problem: CXL Memory Expanders provide high-capacity, high-bandwidth memory but DRAM reliability remains underexplored; traditional RAID/replica-based fault tolerance incurs prohibitive CXL-fabric bandwidth overhead, degrading system performance.
motivation: CXL is emerging for memory capacity/bandwidth expansion, but redundancy mechanisms must avoid saturating the limited CXL interconnect bandwidth.
method: Proposes on-CXL-Memory-Expander-Controller (CXL-MXC) ECC using Locally Recoverable Codes (LRC) as inter-channel ECC (IC-ECC), offloading ECC computation to the CXL expander itself to eliminate redundant CXL fabric traffic. Balances reliability with minimal bandwidth overhead.
key_novelty: Offloading LRC-based ECC to the CXL expander controller to avoid redundant memory access requests in the fabric, achieving reliability without bandwidth amplification.
contributions: LRC-based inter-channel ECC for CXL Memory Expanders
On-expander ECC computation eliminates CXL fabric redundancy
DRAM reliability enhanced 10^9× vs. state-of-art ECC methods
Reduces bandwidth overhead from 63.5% (RAID-CXL) to 3.4%; 12% system performance improvement

metrics.other: Reliability 10^9× improved, bandwidth overhead 63.5%→3.4%, 12% perf gain

limitations: Evaluation scopes limited to CXL-based systems; interaction with PCIe or other interconnect protocols; scaling to heterogeneous workloads; multi-socket implications not discussed.
primary_theme: on-expander LRC-based ECC for CXL Memory bandwidth efficiency
